title: Topological Superconductors in Doubly-Coupled Nanowires with Altermagnetism
summary: We theoretically investigate the possibility of engineering topological superconductivity in doubly coupled nanowires integrating proximity-induced superconductivity and altermagnetism. By tuning experimentally accessible parameters, we find four distinct topological superconducting phases: class D, class BDI, and two phases hosting two Majorana zero modes per end, protected respectively by spin-group and magnetic point-group symmetries. Beyond inheriting the advantages of alternating?magnetism induced topological superconductivity, our system provides multiple tuning knobs (e.g., superconducting phase difference and inter-wire coupling) to control topological properties.

AI.tldr: The paper theoretically explores engineering topological superconductivity in doubly coupled nanowires combining proximity-induced superconductivity and altermagnetism, revealing four distinct topological superconducting phases.
AI.motivation: To investigate how altermagnetism—an emerging magnetic phase—can be combined with coupled nanowire systems to engineer topological superconductivity, expanding beyond conventional approaches and providing more tunable control.
AI.method: Theoretical investigation of doubly coupled nanowires integrating proximity-induced superconductivity and altermagnetism, with tuning of experimentally accessible parameters such as superconducting phase difference and inter-wire coupling.
AI.result: Four distinct topological superconducting phases are found: class D, class BDI, and two phases hosting two Majorana zero modes per end, protected by spin-group and magnetic point-group symmetries respectively.
AI.conclusion: The system inherits the advantages of altermagnetism-induced topological superconductivity while offering multiple tuning knobs (superconducting phase difference, inter-wire coupling) to control topological properties, providing a versatile platform for Majorana-based applications.

title: Imaginary-time correlations in time-sliced stochastic series expansion
summary: Combined with numerical analytic continuation techniques, quantum Monte Carlo (QMC) methods enable the extraction of real-frequency dynamical properties from imaginary-time correlation functions. However, the efficient computation of imaginary-time correlation functions by QMC simulations can (depending on the particular model used) be challenging, particularly for operators that are off-diagonal in the computational basis. In this work, we present an efficient and general algorithm within the stochastic series expansion (SSE) framework for evaluating imaginary-time correlation functions of both diagonal and off-diagonal operators. The algorithm builds on a discrete imaginary-time slicing of the SSE operator string, which provides correlation functions on a grid of well-defined imaginary-time points with no discretization error. For off-diagonal operators, we derive estimators that integrate directly into the existing SSE directed-loop or cluster updating schemes, introducing only minimal computational overhead. We benchmark the method on the one-dimensional transverse-field Ising model (sampling with cluster updates) and XXZ spin chain (using directed-loop sampling), demonstrating excellent agreement (with only statistical errors) with exact diagonalization of small systems. We also study larger systems to demonstrate efficiency.

AI.tldr: This paper presents an efficient and general algorithm within the stochastic series expansion (SSE) framework for computing imaginary-time correlation functions of both diagonal and off-diagonal operators, using discrete imaginary-time slicing of the SSE operator string. Benchmarks on 1D transverse-field Ising and XXZ models show excellent agreement with exact diagonalization.

AI.method: The algorithm uses discrete imaginary-time slicing of the SSE operator string to provide correlation functions on a well-defined imaginary-time grid with no discretization error. AI.conclusion: The proposed SSE-based algorithm offers a general and efficient approach for computing imaginary-time correlation functions of both diagonal and off-diagonal operators, directly compatible with existing update schemes and applicable to larger systems.

title: The principle of stationary action and Lagrangian for dissipative dynamics with velocity-proportional frictional force
summary: It has been known for a long time that the equation of motion for dissipative linear dynamical systems with constant coefficients cannot be derived from the classical principle of stationary action because the term proportional to velocity in the equation of motion leads to the time derivative of order one half in the Lagrangian. Thus, approaches utilising fractional calculus have been used; however, they suffer from deficiencies both from mathematical and physical points of view. We here present our version of such fractional calculus based approach that provides correct Euler-Lagrange and, ultimately, the Hamilton equations, energy change of the moving body, and an attempt for a geometric interpretation of how energy dissipates.

AI.tldr: This paper presents a new fractional calculus-based approach to derive the equations of motion for dissipative linear dynamical systems with constant coefficients. Unlike previous fractional calculus attempts that suffered from mathematical and physical deficiencies, this approach provides correct Euler-Lagrange equations, Hamilton equations, energy change expressions, and a geometric interpretation of energy dissipation.
AI.motivation: The classical principle of stationary action cannot derive equations of motion for dissipative linear dynamical systems with constant coefficients because the velocity-proportional term leads to time derivatives of order one half in the Lagrangian. While fractional calculus has been employed to address this, existing approaches suffer from deficiencies both mathematically and physically, motivating the need for a corrected formulation.
AI.method: The authors present their own version of a fractional calculus-based approach that properly handles the fractional time derivative of order one half arising in the Lagrangian, yielding correct Euler-Lagrange equations and corresponding Hamilton equations from the variational principle.
AI.result: The proposed approach successfully produces correct Euler-Lagrange equations, Hamilton equations, and expressions for the energy change of the moving body in dissipative linear dynamical systems. It also offers a geometric interpretation of how energy dissipates.
AI.conclusion: A consistent fractional calculus framework can be constructed for dissipative linear dynamical systems that resolves the long-standing issue of deriving their equations of motion from a variational principle, complete with energy analysis and a geometric perspective on dissipation.

title: Comparison of mechanical properties of Ag/W1-xTixB2.5 and pure silver coatings deposited by PLD/HIPIMS method
summary: Transition metal borides are attracting increasing interest due to their unique properties. They are not only characterised by very high hardness, but also considerable chemical and thermal stability. Silver, on the other hand, is a good material for increasing electrical and thermal conductivity, wear resistance and has antibacterial properties due to its biological characteristics. Combining these two materials can provide superhard bilayers with increased functional properties. In this study, it was decided to synthesise Ag/WB2.5, Ag/W0.76Ti0.24B2.5 coatings and compare their properties to the individual components. The silver coating was produced by pulsed laser deposition (PLD), while the WB2.5 and W0.76Ti0.24B2.5 coatings were formed by high-power pulsed magnetron sputtering (HiPIMS). To determine the mechanical properties, nanoindentation tests, adhesion of the coatings by scratch -test and wear resistance by abrasion in reciprocating motion were tested. In all cases, the silver film contributed to an increase in the wear resistance of the materials without major changes in the hardness results of the materials. In addition, the Ag/W0.76Ti0.24B2.5 film showed very good adhesion to the substrate. Human hand wiping simulator was also carried out using - Tribotouch. After 36 000 cycles Ag/W0.76Ti0.24B2.5 coating was slightly deformed, which was not visible macroscopically. This result is more than three times greater than for the pure silver film. It was also decided to carry out corrosion tests in an environment of 0.9% NaCl. The Ag/W0.76Ti0.24B2.5 bilayer has very good corrosion resistance, similar to pure silver.

AI.tldr: This study synthesizes Ag/WB2.5 and Ag/W0.76Ti0.24B2.5 bilayer coatings by combining pulsed laser deposition (PLD) for silver and high-power pulsed magnetron sputtering (HiPIMS) for the transition metal borides, and evaluates their mechanical, tribological, and corrosion properties. The silver layer enhances wear resistance without significant hardness loss, the Ag/W0.76Ti0.24B2.5 bilayer shows excellent adhesion, superior durability in human touch simulation, and corrosion resistance comparable to pure silver.
AI.motivation: Transition metal borides offer high hardness and chemical/thermal stability, while silver provides electrical/thermal conductivity, wear resistance, and antibacterial properties. Combining these materials could produce superhard bilayer coatings with enhanced functional properties, and this work investigates such combinations.
AI.method: Ag/WB2.5 and Ag/W0.76Ti0.24B2.5 bilayer coatings were synthesized using PLD for the silver layer and HiPIMS for the boride layers. Properties were assessed via nanoindentation (mechanical properties), scratch testing (adhesion), reciprocating abrasion (wear resistance), a Tribotouch human-hand wiping simulator, and corrosion tests in 0.9% NaCl solution.
AI.result: Silver films improved wear resistance in all cases without significantly altering hardness. Ag/W0.76Ti0.24B2.5 exhibited very good substrate adhesion. In Tribotouch testing, the Ag/W0.76Ti0.24B2.5 coating withstood 36,000 cycles with only slight non-macroscopic deformation—over three times better than pure silver. The bilayer also demonstrated corrosion resistance in 0.9% NaCl comparable to pure silver.
AI.conclusion: Bilayer coatings combining silver with transition metal borides, particularly Ag/W0.76Ti0.24B2.5, provide a favorable balance of wear resistance, adhesion, durability, and corrosion resistance while maintaining hardness, making them promising candidates for functional superhard coating applications.

title: Landau theory and exchange instabilities in Mn$_5$Si$_3$: A case against altermagnetism
summary: Thin-film Mn$_5$Si$_3$ is one of the most studied altermagnetic candidates thanks to its metallicity, demonstrated anomalous transport properties, and assumed $d$-wave exchange splitting pattern enabling spin-polarized transport and various spintronic applications. Its postulated altermagnetic structure has zero propagation vector, in contrast to the collinear antiferromagnetic bulk phase (AFM2) which orders at the $M$ star. In this work, the two phases are analyzed using Landau theories, first-principles calculations of the paramagnetic instabilities, and Monte Carlo simulations. AFM2 appears in a Landau theory as a symmetry-protected inversion-even, permutation-odd mode at a single arm of the $M$ star. At $Γ$, the same intracell ordering pattern belongs to the collinear branch of an $E_{2g}$ order parameter. In both cases, higher-order terms are required for the phase selection. First-principles calculations for the paramagnetic, disordered-local-moment state correctly identify the leading exchange instability at the $M$ star, and the resulting classical Heisenberg model orders at a reasonable temperature into the orthogonal $3M$ phase favored by single-site entropy. The $Γ$-point $E_{2g}$ mode, whose Landau theory contains the altermagnetic sector, is substantially weaker and further suppressed by epitaxial strain representative of Mn$_5$Si$_3$ films exhibiting anomalous transport. The same strain reduces the leading magnetic exchange scale. These results provide a natural explanation for the bulk $M$-point instability but strongly disfavor the postulated relocation of the propagation vector from $M$ to $Γ$ in a moderately strained bulklike Mn$_5$Si$_3$ film, suggesting that the corresponding altermagnetic phase is unlikely to be stabilized without additional physics.

Using Landau theory, first-principles calculations, and Monte Carlo simulations, the authors show that the bulk antiferromagnetic AFM2 phase (M-point) is the natural leading instability, while the Γ-point E₂g altermagnetic mode is substantially weaker and further suppressed by epitaxial strain, casting doubt on the existence of the proposed altermagnetic phase in moderately strained films without additional physics.
AI.motivation: Mn₅Si₃ is a leading altermagnetic candidate due to its metallicity, anomalous transport, and proposed d-wave exchange splitting. However, the postulated altermagnetic phase has zero propagation vector (Γ), conflicting with the bulk collinear antiferromagnetic AFM2 phase that orders at the M star. The authors aim to determine which magnetic instability is truly favored, especially under epitaxial strain conditions relevant to films exhibiting anomalous transport.

The Γ-point E₂g mode (containing the altermagnetic sector) is substantially weaker and is further suppressed by epitaxial strain typical of Mn₅Si₃ films that show anomalous transport. The same strain also reduces the leading magnetic exchange scale.
AI.conclusion: The results naturally explain the bulk M-point magnetic instability but strongly disfavor the relocation of the propagation vector from M to Γ in moderately strained bulklike Mn₅Si₃ films. The postulated altermagnetic phase is unlikely to be stabilized without additional physics (e.g., further symmetry lowering, different strain states, or other mechanisms).
